Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the next steps so we can get your customer-led load test scheduled:

Summary of performance goals you called out:
- Latency: p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 200ms for 512-token prompts (streaming enabled, chunk size ~64 tokens)
- Throughput: sustained 150 requests/sec for steady-state scenarios; burst up to 350 req/sec for short spikes
- Concurrency: support 50–75 concurrent sessions (avg 30 active concurrent)
- Streaming: client requires chunked streaming with first-chunk latency <= 150ms and sustained per-chunk p95 <= 200ms
- Token budgets: typical session ~800–1,200 tokens (prompt + response)

Customer-led load test plan (what we discussed):
- Acme will run k6 (or Locust) from your infra; you’ll share the script and the target test windows
- We’ll provide scoped test API key, endpoint, and IP allowlist to unblock the test
- Redwood will provision capacity and monitor the test (metrics, p95/p99 latency, token throughput, error rates) and stand by for triage

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Please share the k6 script and planned test windows (date/time + timezone)
2) Provide the public IP ranges your test runners will originate from for allowlisting
3) Confirm which model variant you want us to exercise (we suggested redwood-3b for parity with prod)

I attached a short call recap PDF with the SLO table and proposed monitoring dashboards.

If that looks right, Marissa/Laura/Vivek — can you own creating the scoped test key and the initial capacity plan?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
